hypotheses.justification: The statement only mentions `L`, `[Field L]` and `(c : L)`, so `[CharZero L]` is pulled in as an included instance-implicit section variable (all variables of its type, namely `L`, are arguments of the theorem); `[NeZero m]` is already removed by `omit`, and `[NeZero M']`/`ι₀` are not arguments at all since `M'` and `ι₀` are not mentioned. Deleting `CharZero` leaves the statement unchanged and still true: the identity `HahnSeries.C c = algebraMap L (LaurentSeries L) c` for `c : L` is Mathlib's `HahnSeries.C_eq_algebraMap` (`R⟦Γ⟧`'s `Algebra R` structure is defined with `algebraMap := C.comp (algebraMap R A)`, so with `A = R` the two sides are even `rfl`-equal), and it holds for any commutative semiring, in particular for any field, with no characteristic restriction; there are no junk/degenerate cases involved (no division, no truncation), and `L = ℚ` shows the equation is not an artefact of positive characteristic. Concretely, the library's own lemma `ModularCurve.algebraMap_laurentSeries_eq_single` (Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_LaurentCoeff.lean, line 66) is stated with only `(L : Type*) [Field L]` and `(c : L)`, and the existing proof of `C_eq_algebraMap` uses only that lemma together with `HahnSeries.C_apply`; hence the very same proof works after writing `omit [CharZero L] in` in front of the theorem. `[Field L]` itself cannot be deleted (the statement would not elaborate without an algebra/semiring structure on `L`), so `[CharZero L]` is the only removable argument.
